company: Scentre Group (Scentre Group Limited, Scentre Management Limited, RE1 Limited and RE2 Limited as responsible entities of Scentre Group Trusts 1, 2 and 3)
title: Security Trading Policy
date_next_review: Reviewed annually by the Board; no fixed date stated

tiers.name: Scentre Group Directors, officers and employees
tiers.description: Everyone the policy applies to: all Scentre Group Directors and the officers and employees of Scentre Group Limited, Scentre Group Trusts 1, 2 and 3 and their controlled entities. Subject to the Insider Trading Prohibition at all times, but not to blackout periods, clearance, the margin lending ban, the short selling ban or the short-term trading ban, which bite only on Restricted Persons.

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: Specified Persons, Designated Persons, and employees who are likely to have access to confidential information of a 'market sensitive' nature in the ordinary course of their employment. This is the tier that carries the substantive restrictions: no trading in blackout periods, clearance to trade outside them, no margin lending, no short selling, no short-term or speculative trading, and prior Company Secretary approval for other security arrangements over Scentre Group Securities.

tiers.name: Specified Persons
tiers.description: A Scentre Group Director, any executive named as key management personnel in the Group's remuneration report, any Company Secretary, and any other person classified as a Specified Person by the Clearance Committee. Distinguished by clearance from the Clearance Committee (the Chair of the Board and the Chair of the Audit Committee) rather than the CEO.

tiers.name: Designated Persons
tiers.description: Members of the Executive Committee other than Specified Persons, executive assistants and personal assistants of Specified Persons and Executive Committee members, executives and assistants within the legal, secretariat and compliance functions, and any other person notified that they are a Designated Person. Distinguished by clearance from the Chief Executive Officer.

tiers.name: Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: A Scentre Group Director and any executive named as key management personnel in the Group's remuneration report. Used only in section 9(f): for KMP, the excluded-trading carve-out for a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising its rights does not extend to enforcement under a margin lending arrangement.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: The immediate family of a Restricted Person including spouses, partners and children under 18; the trustee of a trust or other fiduciary arrangement under which the Restricted Person is a beneficiary; and any other entity (including family companies, family trusts and personal superannuation funds) over which the Restricted Person or an immediate family member has, or may be expected to have, investment control or influence, including as trustee, shareholder or unitholder. The Restricted Person must inform them, communicate with the Clearance Officer for them, and ensure their compliance.

definitions.hedging_definition: hedging arrangements in respect of unvested awards or awards that have vested but are held in a holding lock or otherwise the subject of deferral of delivery offered under the equity-linked incentive plans operated by Scentre Group

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may extend a blackout period or specify any additional period as a blackout period. Separately, the Chief Executive Officer has discretion to impose ad hoc restrictions on certain employees at times when matters subject to ASX Listing Rule 3.1A are being considered by employees directly involved in or with knowledge of those matters. The policy does not say either is announced, and a person refused clearance must keep the refusal confidential.

rules.detail: Exchange-traded options, warrants, futures and other Financial Products issued over Scentre Group Securities and able to be traded on a financial market are themselves Scentre Group Securities, so trading them requires prior written clearance and is barred in blackout periods. Any such derivative must not be short-term or speculative under 11(d), and clearance will be refused if the request rests on short-term or speculative considerations.
rules.evidence: any Financial Products issued over or in respect of the above securities which are able to be traded on a financial market.

rules.detail: A bilateral OTC put and call with a bank is arguably outside limb (d) of Scentre Group Securities, which is confined to Financial Products 'able to be traded on a financial market', so the clearance and blackout machinery may not reach it on its own terms. But 11(d) expressly regulates 'derivative or other Financial Products issued over or in respect of Scentre Group Securities' without that market-traded limitation, and Financial Product expressly includes options, forward contracts and swaps. The prudent and evidently intended reading is that an OTC collar is caught and needs clearance; it is prohibited if short-term or speculative.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not engage in short-term or speculative trading in Scentre Group Securities or in derivative or other Financial Products issued over or is respect of Scentre Group Securities.

rules.detail: Executives participating in the equity-linked incentive plans are prohibited from hedging unvested awards. The operative detail sits in a separate document, the Hedging of Executive Awards and Performance Rights Policy, which is not part of this policy and must be obtained separately.
rules.evidence: Prohibitions also apply to executives participating in the equity-linked incentive plans from entering into hedging arrangements in respect of unvested awards ... These prohibitions are outlined in the Scentre Group's Hedging of Executive Awards and Performance Rights Policy.

rules.detail: The ban is expressly extended past vesting: awards that have vested but are held in a holding lock or are otherwise subject to deferral of delivery cannot be hedged. This closes the usual gap between vesting and release for plan securities.
rules.evidence: hedging arrangements in respect of unvested awards or awards that have vested but are held in a holding lock or otherwise the subject of deferral of delivery offered under the equity-linked incentive plans operated by Scentre Group.

rules.detail: The hedging prohibition is carefully bounded: it reaches unvested awards and vested awards still in a holding lock or subject to deferred delivery, and stops there. Shares that have vested and been released, and ordinary on-market holdings, are not covered by any hedging ban in this policy. Hedging them is regulated only as trading: prior written clearance from the relevant Clearance Officer, outside blackout periods, not short-term or speculative, and subject to whatever the separate Hedging of Executive Awards and Performance Rights Policy says.
rules.evidence: Prohibitions also apply to executives participating in the equity-linked incentive plans from entering into hedging arrangements in respect of unvested awards or awards that have vested but are held in a holding lock or otherwise the subject of deferral of delivery

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or collar-plus-loan over released shares is a transaction associated with disposing of or agreeing to dispose of Scentre Group Securities and so is a trade requiring prior written clearance; the secured loan leg additionally needs the Company Secretary's prior approval under 11(b). It must not be short-term (under three months) or speculative.
rules.evidence: “deal” or “trade” includes to take part in any transaction associated with buying, selling, acquiring, disposing of, converting or agreeing to do any of those things

rules.detail: Flat ban with no definition, no carve-out and no clearance route. Because it is undefined, a physically settled short leg or a cash-settled position taken without holding the underlying could be characterised as short selling.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not engage in short selling of Scentre Group Securities.

rules.detail: Securities lending is nowhere named, is not listed in the definition of deal or trade, and is not among the excluded dealings. A title-transfer stock loan would involve a disposal and so be a trade, but the policy does not say so.

Contracts for difference are expressly named as Financial Products, and 11(d) regulates derivative and other Financial Products issued over or in respect of Scentre Group Securities. A CFD is therefore permitted only with prior written clearance and only if not short-term (under three months) or speculative, which in practice will bar most CFD positions; a short CFD would also engage the short selling ban.
rules.evidence: Financial Product means any financial instrument, including derivatives, options, warrants, futures, forward contracts, swaps and contracts for difference.

rules.detail: Flat ban on entering margin lending arrangements in relation to Scentre Group Securities, with no clearance or waiver route. The ban is confined to 'all arrangements properly described as margin lending arrangements'; the Company Secretary is the arbiter of whether a given arrangement is a margin loan or merely a security arrangement.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons may not enter into margin lending arrangements in relation to Scentre Group Securities.

rules.detail: Granting a security interest over Scentre Group Securities is not a 'trade' under the deal/trade definition and is not caught by the margin lending ban, but the policy imposes a standalone requirement of prior approval from the Company Secretary before entering into any such security arrangement. Approval is by the Company Secretary alone, not the Clearance Committee or CEO.
rules.evidence: However, if a Restricted Person proposes to enter into any such security arrangement they should obtain the prior approval of the Company Secretary prior to entering into any such arrangement.

rules.detail: The policy draws an express and unusual line: the ban stops at margin lending and does not extend to other types of loan secured by a security interest over Scentre Group Securities. A term loan from a bank secured on collared shares is therefore permitted, conditional on prior approval from the Company Secretary, who is also the person to consult on whether the facility is properly classified as margin lending.
rules.evidence: The above restriction includes all arrangements properly described as margin lending arrangements but does not extend to other types of loan arrangements which may be secured by a security interest granted in respect of Scentre Group Securities.

rules.detail: Short-term or speculative trading is banned in Scentre Group Securities and in derivatives or other Financial Products issued over or in respect of them; short-term means in less than a 3-month period. Reinforced at the clearance stage: clearance will not be given where the request is based on considerations of a short-term or speculative nature. No carve-outs are stated, including for plan securities.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not engage in short-term or speculative trading in Scentre Group Securities or in derivative or other Financial Products issued over or is respect of Scentre Group Securities. Short-term means in less than a 3-month period.

rules.detail: KMP may take a non-margin loan secured over Scentre Group Securities with the Company Secretary's prior approval, and for such a facility a disposal resulting from the secured lender exercising its rights is excluded trading. The KMP-specific carve-back in 9(f) removes that protection only for enforcement under a margin lending arrangement, which KMP cannot enter in any event.
rules.evidence: a disposal of Scentre Group Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights. For the avoidance of doubt, in relation to Key Management Personnel, this does not extend to the exercise by a lender of rights under a margin lending arrangement;

clearance.approver: Clearance Committee (the Chair of the Board and the Chair of the Audit Committee; if a member is absent or is the applicant, the remaining member plus a Director nominated by the Chair of the Board), via a Securities Dealing Request Form sent to the Company Secretary
clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary; for Scentre Group Directors also in time for a Listing Rule 3.19A notice to be prepared and announced to ASX
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within two business days of the trade occurring
clearance.evidence: Specified Persons may only trade in Scentre Group Securities outside a blackout period if they have received prior written consent from the Clearance Committee. ... must complete the trade within three business days of the clearance being received, and fresh approval must be sought for any trades after this clearance period.

clearance.approver: Chief Executive Officer, via a Securities Dealing Request Form sent to the Company Secretary
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within two business days of the trade occurring
clearance.evidence: Designated Persons may only trade in Scentre Group Securities outside a blackout period if they have received prior written consent from the Chief Executive Officer.

clearance.approver: Chief Financial Officer or Company Secretary for Restricted Persons who are neither Specified nor Designated Persons; for any security arrangement over Scentre Group Securities, the Company Secretary specifically
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within two business days of the trade occurring
clearance.evidence: Clearance Officer means in relation to: Specified Persons, the Clearance Committee; Designated Persons, the Chief Executive Officer; and other Scentre Group employees prescribed as “Restricted Persons”, the Chief Financial Officer or Company Secretary.

clearance.approver: The Clearance Officer of the associated Restricted Person; the Restricted Person must communicate on the Associate's behalf
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within two business days of the trade occurring
clearance.evidence: a Restricted Person must inform their Associates about this policy and communicate on behalf of their Associates with the relevant Clearance Officer for the purposes of this policy and the Restricted Person must ensure compliance with this policy by its Associates.

clearance.tier: Scentre Group Directors, officers and employees
clearance.evidence: Specific clearance requirements for Restricted Persons to trade Scentre Group Securities outside blackout periods are set out in section 5.

short_term.basis: short-term means in less than a 3-month period; applies to trading in Scentre Group Securities and in derivatives or other Financial Products issued over or in respect of them
short_term.evidence: Restricted Persons must not engage in short-term or speculative trading in Scentre Group Securities or in derivative or other Financial Products issued over or is respect of Scentre Group Securities.  Short-term means in less than a 3-month period.

exceptions.evidence: transfers where the beneficial interest in the relevant Scentre Group Securities does not change (e.g. the transfer from one personal security holding to another).

exceptions.evidence: indirect or incidental trading that occurs as a consequence of an investment in, or trading in securities of a managed investment scheme, listed investment company, exchange traded fund or similar investment vehicle (other than a vehicle investing only in Scentre Group Securities) that is managed by a third party

where a Restricted Person is a trustee, trading in the Scentre Group Securities by that trust provided that the Restricted Person is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to trade during the blackout period is taken by the other trustee(s) or by the investment managers independently of the Restricted Person;

a disposal of Scentre Group Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights. For the avoidance of doubt, in relation to Key Management Personnel, this does not extend to the exercise by a lender of rights under a margin lending arrangement;
the acquisition (but not the sale) of securities under the Group’s Performance Rights Plan where the acquisition is during a blackout period;

exceptions.approver: Relevant Clearance Officer (prior written clearance for the plan itself)
exceptions.evidence: an acquisition or disposal of Scentre Group Securities under a pre-determined investment or divestment plan for which prior written clearance has been provided ... and where: (i) the Restricted Person did not enter into the plan or amend the plan during the blackout period; and (ii) the trading plan does not permit the Restricted Person to exercise any influence or discretion over how, when, or whether to trade.

exceptions.approver: Clearance Officer (Clearance Committee for Specified Persons; CEO for Designated Persons; CFO or Company Secretary for other Restricted Persons)
exceptions.evidence: A clearance to trade (“exceptional circumstances notice”) may be given to a Restricted Person, who is not in possession of unpublished market sensitive information, during a blackout period if he or she is in severe financial hardship ... An exceptional circumstances notice may only be given in respect of the sale (but not purchase) of Scentre Group Securities.

is the subject of a court order or court enforceable undertaking or where there are other exceptional circumstances ... A circumstance may be considered exceptional if the person in question is required by a court order to transfer or sell the Scentre Group Securities or there is some other overriding legal or regulatory requirement for that person to do so.

financing_disclosure: Restricted Persons (including Specified Persons, Designated Persons and Key Management Personnel): at inception of any loan arrangement secured by a security interest granted in respect of Scentre Group Securities that is not a margin lending arrangement, prior approval must be obtained from the Company Secretary before entering into the arrangement (section 11(b)).
Restricted Persons: consult the Company Secretary where uncertain whether an arrangement is properly classified as a margin lending or security arrangement (section 11(b)).

Specified Persons and Designated Persons: after any trade, notify the Company Secretary within two business days; Scentre Group Directors within sufficient time for a Listing Rule 3.19A notice to be prepared and announced to ASX (section 5.3).

exemption_authority: No general exemption power. The only relief from blackout periods is an exceptional circumstances notice under section 6, which can be issued only by a Clearance Officer (the Clearance Committee for Specified Persons, the CEO for Designated Persons, the CFO or Company Secretary for other Restricted Persons), only to a person not holding unpublished market sensitive information, only for severe financial hardship, a court order or court enforceable undertaking or other exceptional circumstances, and only in respect of a sale, not a purchase. Clearance Officers are told to exercise the discretion with caution if in any doubt, and Scentre Group may have to notify the nature of the exceptional circumstances to ASX. No one is given power to waive the margin lending, short selling or short-term trading prohibitions in section 11.
jurisdiction_overlays: ASX Listing Rule 12.10 (lodgement), Listing Rule 3.19A (Director interest notices) and Listing Rules 3.1 / 3.1A (basis for the CEO's ad hoc restrictions)
Stapled structure: the policy covers Scentre Group stapled securities and, separately, units in the Carindale Property Trust, each with its own blackout calendar

bespoke_clauses.clause: The above restriction includes all arrangements properly described as margin lending arrangements but does not extend to other types of loan arrangements which may be secured by a security interest granted in respect of Scentre Group Securities. However, if a Restricted Person proposes to enter into any such security arrangement they should obtain the prior approval of the Company Secretary prior to entering into any such arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the clause that makes a funded collar feasible: a bank term loan secured on the collared securities is expressly outside the margin lending ban and needs only the Company Secretary's prior approval, so the financing leg has a defined, single-approver route.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Restricted Person should also consult with the Company Secretary if they are uncertain as to whether an arrangement is properly classified as a margin lending or security arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Company Secretary decides whether the facility is 'properly described as' margin lending, so the loan should be documented with no LVR-based margin call or top-up mechanics and the characterisation confirmed in writing before signing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of Scentre Group Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights. For the avoidance of doubt, in relation to Key Management Personnel, this does not extend to the exercise by a lender of rights under a margin lending arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Enforcement or physical settlement by the bank under a non-margin secured facility is excluded from the blackout and trading restrictions even for directors and KMP, so the bank's security can be realised in a blackout period without putting the executive in breach; the carve-back bites only on margin lending, which is prohibited anyway.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging ban is bounded to plan securities
bespoke_clauses.clause: Prohibitions also apply to executives participating in the equity-linked incentive plans from entering into hedging arrangements in respect of unvested awards or awards that have vested but are held in a holding lock or otherwise the subject of deferral of delivery.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no hedging prohibition on vested, released or ordinarily acquired securities, so a collar over unrestricted shares is not barred by this policy, but shares still in a holding lock or subject to deferred delivery must be excluded from the collar pool.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging rules sit outside this policy
bespoke_clauses.clause: These prohibitions are outlined in the Group's Hedging of Executive Awards and Performance Rights Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The operative hedging restrictions are in a separate document not lodged with this policy, so that policy must be reviewed before any collar is priced; it may be wider than the summary given here.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must not engage in short-term or speculative trading in Scentre Group Securities or in derivative or other Financial Products issued over or is respect of Scentre Group Securities. Short-term means in less than a 3-month period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The ban expressly reaches derivatives over the securities, so a collar must have a tenor of at least three months and should not contain early unwind or knock-out features that would make it short-term in substance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: clearance to trade will not be given where the request to trade is based on considerations of a short-term or speculative nature
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The clearance application should present the collar as long-term risk management of a concentrated holding rather than a view on the price, since the Clearance Officer must refuse anything framed as short-term or speculative.

bespoke_clauses.topic: OTC products may fall outside the Securities definition
bespoke_clauses.clause: Scentre Group Securities means ... any Financial Products issued over or in respect of the above securities which are able to be traded on a financial market.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bilateral OTC collar may not be 'able to be traded on a financial market' and so may sit outside the clearance and blackout machinery on the literal wording, but section 11(d) regulates derivatives over the securities without that limit, so clearance should be sought regardless rather than relying on the gap.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a clearance to trade can be withdrawn if new information comes to light or if there is a change in circumstances ... must complete the trade within three business days of the clearance being received, and fresh approval must be sought for any trades after this clearance period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar must be priced and executed within three business days of clearance, and clearance can be pulled before execution, so the bank's mandate should contemplate silent withdrawal and re-approval for any roll or restructure.

bespoke_clauses.clause: if the clearance to trade is refused, the person seeking clearance must keep that information confidential.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The executive cannot tell the bank why the trade cannot proceed, so documentation should not require a reason to be given for withdrawal.

bespoke_clauses.topic: brokers with discretion must be notified
bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must also inform their brokers or financial advisers who have discretion to trade on their behalf that the Restricted Person is restricted from trading Scentre Group Securities under this policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If any part of the structure gives the bank discretionary dealing authority over the securities, the bank must be formally notified of the trading restrictions.

bespoke_clauses.clause: any other entity (including family companies, family trusts and personal superannuation funds) over which the Restricted Person or Restricted Person's immediate family member has, or may be expected to have, investment control or influence (including in its capacity as trustee or shareholder or unitholder)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Booking the collar or the loan in a family trust, SMSF or personal company does not avoid clearance, the blackout periods or the section 11 prohibitions.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the Chief Executive Officer has discretion to impose ad hoc restrictions on certain employees at times when matters subject to ASX Listing Rule 3.1A are being considered
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Entry, roll or unwind can be blocked at any time outside the scheduled blackout calendar and without public notice, so execution timing cannot be guaranteed to the counterparty.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A blackout period is: (a) in respect of stapled securities of Scentre Group: the period commencing on 1 July ... and the period commencing on 1 January ...; and (b) in respect of units in the Carindale Property Trust: ...
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Scentre Group stapled securities are effectively closed from 1 January and 1 July until two hours after the relevant results release, leaving only narrow open windows in which a collar can be entered, amended or unwound.

summary: A funded collar over vested, released Scentre Group stapled securities is possible under this policy, and it is one of the more accommodating policies for the structure. There is no general hedging ban: section 10(b) prohibits hedging only of unvested awards and of awards that have vested but remain in a holding lock or subject to deferral of delivery, so unrestricted holdings are outside it, although the separate Hedging of Executive Awards and Performance Rights Policy must be reviewed because the operative prohibitions live there. Critically, section 11(b) confines the margin lending ban to arrangements properly described as margin lending and expressly permits other loan arrangements secured by a security interest over Scentre Group Securities, subject only to the prior approval of the Company Secretary, and section 9(f) treats a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising its rights as excluded trading even for Key Management Personnel, with the carve-back applying only to margin lending. The conditions are that the derivative legs and any share disposal need prior written clearance from the Clearance Committee (Specified Persons, including Directors and KMP) or the CEO (Designated Persons), must be executed within three business days of clearance and outside the 1 January and 1 July blackout periods and any Board or CEO ad hoc restriction, must be notified to the Company Secretary within two business days (and in time for a Listing Rule 3.19A notice for Directors), and the facility must be documented so that it is not a margin loan and the collar has a tenor of at least three months and is not presented as short-term or speculative, since clearance must be refused on that ground.
